lead.title: Pretzel Therapeutics gets MHRA clearance for the Phase II POLARIS trial of PX578, a POLG activator
lead.deck: This is the third regulatory milestone in a few months for the small molecule, after FDA IND clearance (Aug 2026) and Fast Track (Sept 2026). The randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial will assess safety, PK/PD and efficacy in adults with POLG disease; start targeted by end-2026.

milestone.title: Servier: sevasemten, acquired with Edgewise's business, misses its primary endpoint in Becker muscular dystrophy
milestone.summary: The 18-month, placebo-controlled Phase II GRAND CANYON trial missed its primary endpoint, the NSAA score, and its secondary endpoints; the safety profile remains favorable.
milestone.why: Servier paid $1.55B upfront (plus up to $1.1B in milestones) for this asset: a reminder of clinical risk in mid-stage asset buyouts, useful to calibrate Phase II biotech valuations.

deal.thesis: Boehringer licenses six preclinical oncology programs (ADCs and T-cell engagers, five from LaNova) with up to $7B in milestones: European big pharma keeps buying Chinese innovation very early, a comparable for European ADC/TCE biotechs.

brefsEurope.title: bit.bio raises $25M Series D for its programmed human cells
brefsEurope.summary: With existing investor M&G Investments and Abcam founder Jonathan Milner. The opti-ox platform produces 50+ cell types (ioCells: heart, liver, CNS); funds go to broadening the catalog and commercial growth.

brefsEurope.title: Vitroscope raises $7M to turn living human tissue into a drug discovery data source
brefsEurope.summary: Norwegian startup working on vascularized organoids and intact tissues kept under flow, to study drug effects and immune response.

brefsEurope.title: Lonza buys five US manufacturing sites from Merck KGaA (bioconjugates, viral vectors, LNPs)
brefsEurope.summary: Enterprise value in the low-to-mid triple-digit millions of CHF, closing expected mid-2027; about 1,100 employees and CHF 250M of 2028 sales expected. A demand signal for ADC and viral-vector capacity.

brefsEurope.title: AbbVie licenses a gut-selective EP4 agonist for IBD from Nxera ($100M upfront) and expands its Oxford site
brefsEurope.summary: Up to $1.37B in milestones for NXE0033744, in Phase I; AbbVie announces £120M of UK investment, including a new 12,000 sq ft site in Oxford.

word.definition: A 3D structure grown from stem cells or patient tissue that reproduces part of an organ's architecture and function to test drugs.

parts.label: Source cells
parts.role: stem cells or a patient biopsy

parts.label: Readout
parts.role: imaging, omics or AI to measure response

how.t: Stem cells or a tissue fragment are placed in a 3D matrix with growth factors.
Cells assemble into micro-structures close to the original organ, sometimes with flow or vascularization.
The organoid is exposed to the drug, then toxicity and efficacy are measured, often with AI.

word.why: Regulators encourage animal-free alternatives and industry wants more predictive models: organoids lower clinical failure risk, hence a stream of rounds on the 'discovery data' layer. Watch consolidation (MIMETAS, majority-acquired by Bruker in August 2026).
